meta.title: kerlico: a single-binary proxy core written in Rust
meta.description: kerlico is a proxy core written in Rust. One executable acts as client, server or both according to its JSON configuration. 30 protocol modules. GPL-3.0-only.
hero.tag: A proxy core written in Rust. One executable acts as client, server or both, as its JSON configuration says.
roles.title: One file, two roles
roles.lead: `apps/kerlico` links crates split by responsibility and protocol into one executable. The configuration decides which side runs.
roles.both_path: A single `Engine` holds local inbounds, server nodes and the named outbound table together.
roles.trim: At build time, Cargo features remove protocols. At run time, `Registry` looks up the registered factory by the `type` in the configuration.
roles.ref: The design draws on mihomo, sing-box and Xray-core. The configuration format is JSON v2. The workspace lint is `unsafe_code = "forbid"`.
disp.title: One Dispatcher
disp.lead: An `Engine` assembles exactly one `EgressRuntime` / `Dispatcher`. Every inbound hands its target request to it after authentication, and each named outbound is built once.
disp.aria: Architecture diagram: inbound nodes and the local inbound converge on one Dispatcher, which first splits into Local and Remote. Local splits into IPv4, IPv6 and WARP fill-in. Remote carries the original domain to the selected remote proxy.
disp.s1: IPv4 and IPv6 nodes are created separately, each with its own `NodeId`, listen address, credentials, quota and cancellation scope. Reusing a secret across nodes is rejected when the configuration compiles.
disp.s2: `Dispatcher` branches on the selected named outbound's `TargetPolicy`. With no rule match it uses the node's bound outbound. A TCP connection or UDP association fixes its outbound when it opens and never switches.
disp.s3_t: Local: resolve here, pick a family
disp.s3: The node's `ipv4-only`, `ipv6-only` or `dual-stack` mode (IPv4 first by default) selects the target address and exit. With `device` configured, `dual-stack` reaches a missing address family through WARP.
disp.s4: The website domain or IP, port and payload go to the selected remote proxy in its wire format, and this machine does not resolve the website domain. On remote failure the session returns a protocol error or ends. It does not change family, change proxy or fall back to direct.
wall.title: 30 protocol modules
wall.lead: `kerlico modules` lists the modules registered in this build as `outbound/<type>` and `inbound/<type>`. The default build contains all 30 below.
wall.hint: Hover, focus or tap a face to see its direction and a note.
proto.vless: Transport, security, Encryption, Vision and packet encoding assemble separately. Invalid combinations are rejected at configuration time.
proto.vmess: VMess AEAD. The node member credential is the protocol UUID.
proto.trojan: TCP CONNECT and UDP ASSOCIATE. UDP is carried inside the stream.
proto.shadowsocks: AEAD and Legacy methods. SS2022 is a separate module.
proto.ss2022: Three `2022-blake3-*` methods. TCP uses stream primitives and UDP uses native crypto primitives.
proto.shadowsocksr: Protocols cover origin, auth_sha1_v4, auth_aes128, auth_chain_a/b.
proto.anytls: `--features anytls` enables both ends on its own.
proto.shadowtls: A composite stream wrapper. It only builds paths with a real inner protocol.
proto.snell: Outbound v4, node v5, v6 on both ends. v5 QUIC Proxy Mode is not implemented.
proto.tuic: v4 and v5 on both ends. Each new QUIC connection gets its own token cache.
proto.hysteria1: Wire version `0x03`. The node listens on QUIC/UDP.
proto.hysteria2: HTTP/3 authentication, plain QUIC and Salamander carriers, BBR and NewReno congestion settings.
proto.shadowquic: Member identity comes from the user the JLS library returns after real authentication.
proto.mieru: TCP node identity comes from the Key that first decrypts successfully, not from the user hint in the nonce.
proto.naive: Each H1, H2 or H3 CONNECT creates a peer from the member matched by Basic auth.
proto.trusttunnel: H1, H2 and H3 CONNECT. Each `_udp2` target flow inherits the same user.
proto.sudoku: raw, legacy and split modes authenticate with AEAD/KIP against a candidate table.
proto.socks: Versions 4, 4a and 5. Only version 5 offers UDP Associate.
proto.http: Nodes handle HTTP/1.1 CONNECT and plain HTTP request forwarding, with optional TLS.
proto.wireguard: `boringtun` plus `smoltcp`, entirely in user space, with no system TUN device.
proto.tun: Creates a kernel TUN interface. It belongs in `local_inbounds`, needs `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and leaves system routes alone.
proto.ssh: Native Rust SSH v2 `direct-tcpip`. TCP only, no UDP.
proto.gost-relay: Outbound CONNECT only. TCP and fixed-target UDP travel over a TCP stream.
proto.tor: Embeds `arti-client`, needs no external Tor daemon, and reaches public v3 `.onion` targets.
proto.masque: HTTP/3 CONNECT-IP (RFC 9484), with no system TUN device.
proto.openvpn: Native OpenVPN 2.x client. It does not start an `openvpn` process.
proto.openconnect: Native AnyConnect client. Traffic uses CSTP over TLS, without DTLS.
proto.tailscale: Joins a tailnet with a pre-auth key. It does not start `tailscaled`.
proto.easytier: Joins an EasyTier network as an ordinary peer, with no system TUN device.
proto.zerotier: A native Rust node joins a private network. It does not start `zerotier-one`.
tun.title: Tunnel and overlay outbounds
tun.lead: Six native Rust clients attach remote networks as named outbounds that nodes or rules reference by `tag`. One user-space `ClientTunnel` handles their IP packets, with no system TUN device.
tun.masque: HTTP/3 CONNECT-IP (RFC 9484). TCP, fixed-target UDP and multi-target UDP associations on one exit.
tun.openvpn: OpenVPN 2.x client. UDP and TCP carriers. Data channel AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM or CHACHA20-POLY1305.
tun.openconnect: AnyConnect protocol client. Traffic uses CSTP over TLS, without DTLS. Peer tested: `ocserv` 1.1.6.
tun.tailscale: Joins a tailnet with a pre-auth key. Interop testing uses `headscale` 0.27.1 and official `tailscale` 1.92.3. The official SaaS control plane is untested.
tun.easytier: Joins as an ordinary peer to reach virtual IPs and subnet proxies other nodes advertise. Only this module needs `protoc` at build time.
tun.zerotier: A native node joins a private network. The protocol code is translated from `node/` in ZeroTierOne 1.16.2 and lives in `third_party/zerotier-node`, MPL-2.0.
tun.note: Targets must be reachable through that network. Domains are resolved on this machine.
users.title: Users and statistics
users.lead: Payload bytes are counted once, at the logical channel `Dispatcher` returns. The same increment projects onto four views, and the views do not add up to each other.
users.meter_aria: A packet passes the single metering boundary. One count projects onto the Engine, UserId, NodeId and OutId views.
users.a1: `AccountSpec` holds an immutable `UserId`, a username in `<prefix>_<uuid>` form by default, and an Argon2id digest. Renaming or rotating credentials keeps the `UserId`.
users.a2: Node `members` bind `user_id` to `native_credential`. The management password digest never acts as a protocol password, and wire formats stay unchanged.
users.a3: TLS/QUIC handshakes, multiplexing control frames, WireGuard headers and retransmissions stay out of payload traffic. `CarrierUsage` or device metrics count them.
users.a4: With `telemetry` configured, usage, bandwidth, access records, DNS and error events go to SQLite. Query them read-only with `kerlico history --kind usage|flows|bandwidth|events`.
users.a5: The `control` section opens a read-only HTTP API: health, usage, online, access records and counters.
start.title: Get started
start.dl: Download the Linux `x86_64` `kerlico` from Releases and verify it with `SHA256SUMS`. It needs glibc 2.34 or later.
start.c_check: Validates the configuration without listening on any port.
start.c_run: Starts, and exits gracefully on `Ctrl-C` or `SIGTERM`.
start.c_modules: Lists the protocols in this build.
start.src: Building from source needs Rust `1.99.1`: `cargo build --locked --release -p kerlico`.
start.cli_lang: CLI output comes only in `zh-CN` and `en`, selected with `--lang`. The usage guide exists in Chinese and English. Interface docs are in Chinese only.
start.l3: TUN is verified on Linux only and leaves routes alone. It sees only IP targets, so domain rules do not match.
start.l4: The WARP data plane is verified on a dual-stack machine. The CLI's automatic fill-in on a real single-stack machine is untested.
start.l5: ShadowQUIC v2 does not interoperate with the pinned Mihomo version.
start.l6: Outbound selection groups (Policy Group) are not implemented yet.
start.rel: 1.3.1 fix: one UDP packet from a disabled member could stop an SS2022, Shadowsocks or ShadowsocksR node. The packet is now dropped.
